note: Machine-readable index of every runnable lab. The prep site (prep-preview) reads a copy of this file; edit HERE and run prep-preview/scripts/sync-labs.mjs.

tracks.title: Runtime debugging
tracks.summary: 16 classic C/C++ bugs: reproduce, locate with gdb / valgrind / sanitizers, separate crash site from root cause, fix.
tracks.run: ./build.sh then open the files in numeric order

tracks.title: LLVM IR debugging
tracks.summary: Drop below C: follow a bug through IR, bitcode, debugify, llc and gdb; learn what the verifier cannot see.

tracks.title: Source ↔ IR ↔ asm
tracks.summary: One crash at every level; walk from the faulting register up to the source line and backward to the root cause; -O0 vs -O2.

tracks.title: Measurement & profiling
tracks.summary: Noise floor, hardware counters, sampling down to the hot source line, microbenchmark traps, tail latency. Every number reproduced on the lab machine.
tracks.run: cd perf && ./build.sh, then follow each file's STEP commands

tracks.title: Memory hierarchy & data layout
tracks.summary: Cache lines, the L1/L2/L3/DRAM staircase and the TLB cliff, AoS vs SoA, false sharing, memory-level parallelism, huge pages.

tracks.title: Source → IR → asm → microarchitecture
tracks.summary: What idioms compile to, vectorizer remarks, llvm-mca predictions checked against the machine, branch vs select, LTO and inlining.
tracks.run: cd codegen && ./build.sh (emits the .s files the labs read)

tracks.title: Atomics, memory ordering, lock-free
tracks.summary: A race TSan sees, an SPSC queue three ways, every memory_order on x86 and AArch64, lock costs with futex counts, the store-buffer litmus test.

tracks.title: Allocation, syscalls, networking
tracks.summary: malloc as a distribution, the syscall floor and vDSO, blocking vs epoll vs busy-poll, the Nagle stall, kernel receive timestamps.

tracks.title: AArch64 codegen & dispatch (emulated)
tracks.summary: Root-free cross toolchain + qemu; Arm asm next to x86, NEON vs SVE at five vector lengths, LSE and outline atomics, ifunc dispatch, SME first look.

tracks.title: Unfamiliar large codebases
tracks.summary: Build topology from Ninja and the compile database, ELF forensics, reading flags off binaries, profiling a program whose time lives in shared libraries (with the two classic mis-profiles), compile-time investigation with -ftime-trace. Subject: the local LLVM build and the distro clang.
tracks.run: bigcode/run_bigcode.sh (labs are markdown with the real outputs)

tracks.title: End-to-end investigations
tracks.summary: Capstone 0 worked in full (why does a translation unit take three seconds?); templates for a public x86 codebase investigation and for NEON vs SVE kernel selection validated under emulation.
tracks.run: read capstones/README.md; do capstones 1 and 2 on your own public code

labs.title: Null pointer dereference
labs.evidence: gdb backtrace naming the faulting line; ASan report classifying the access

labs.title: Uninitialized / wild pointer (nondeterministic UB)
labs.evidence: Exit codes from 16 runs differ; deterministic under setarch -R; valgrind silent because the address is mapped

labs.title: Integer divide by zero (SIGFPE)
labs.evidence: x/i $pc shows idiv; UBSan names file:line:col

labs.title: Stack array out-of-bounds write
labs.evidence: Plain run silent; canary aborts at return; ASan points at the write; valgrind misses it

labs.title: Heap buffer overflow
labs.evidence: ASan heap-buffer-overflow with allocation stack

labs.title: Use after free
labs.evidence: valgrind: use / free / alloc sites; ASan heap-use-after-free

labs.title: Double free
labs.evidence: glibc abort backtrace; ASan attempting double-free with both free stacks

labs.title: Memory leak
labs.evidence: valgrind definitely-lost record with allocation stack; LSan report

labs.title: Use of uninitialized value
labs.evidence: valgrind conditional-jump-depends-on-uninitialised with origin

labs.title: Returning a pointer to a local
labs.evidence: ASan stack-use-after-return (with detect_stack_use_after_return)

labs.title: Infinite recursion / stack overflow
labs.evidence: gdb giant backtrace; bt -5 shows the base; ASan stack-overflow

labs.title: Signed integer overflow (UB)
labs.evidence: UBSan runtime error; -O2 changes the observable result

labs.title: Call through a null function pointer
labs.evidence: gdb stops at address 0; frame 1 names the caller

labs.title: Off-by-one heap over-read
labs.evidence: Invalid read 1 byte past the block

labs.title: free() of a non-heap pointer
labs.evidence: glibc invalid pointer abort; ASan attempting free on address not malloc()-ed

labs.title: C++ pitfalls: operator[] vs at(), new/delete UAF, delete[] mismatch
labs.evidence: Four demos: assertion, exception, ASan UAF, ASan alloc-dealloc-mismatch

labs.title: Follow a C bug down the pipeline: IR, bitcode, debugify, llc, gdb
labs.evidence: gdb maps the fault to a real C line (Track A) and to an IR instruction ordinal (Track B)

labs.title: Hand-written IR: verifier says VALID, program crashes
labs.evidence: verify passes; native and lli runs SIGSEGV; debugify pins IR line 10

labs.title: Rosetta Stone: one store at source, IR and asm
labs.evidence: 3-row map: C line, IR store i32 43981, movl $0xabcd,(%rax) with rax = 0

labs.title: The debugify line-number trap
labs.evidence: gdb says .ll:29 but the physical line 29 is innocent; map via !DILocation

labs.title: Crash site vs root cause: walk the SSA def-use chain backward
labs.evidence: Faulting store traced back to the trunc; valgrind names the uninitialised half in the C analogue

labs.title: The same bug at -O0 vs -O2: UB deleted to unreachable
labs.evidence: -O0 crashes cleanly; -O2 main is a single unreachable; a local becomes <optimized out>

labs.title: The noise floor: pin, warm up, hybrid cores, cycles vs time
labs.evidence: Your own min/p50/p99 unpinned vs P-core vs E-core; cycles/iteration from perf stat matches the dependent-chain latency

labs.title: Hardware counters: branch misses, IPC, demand vs prefetched misses
labs.evidence: sorted vs random: same instructions, ~24 cycles per mispredict; stride-1 vs stride-16: prefetcher hides misses

labs.title: From a slow binary to the hot source line (inlining, mangling, stripped binaries)
labs.evidence: Hot lines 119-121 found inside main; inlined frames shown; stripped binary symbolized via .debug file; one address resolved to fnv1a:121

labs.title: Microbenchmark pitfalls: DCE, constant folding, closed forms, volatile, warm-up, timer cost
labs.evidence: Disassembly proves each 0 ms row; volatile 8x slower than the shipped loop; timer costs measured

labs.title: Tail latency: histograms, page faults, preemption, pre-faulting
labs.evidence: p99.9 from ~39 us to ~7.6 us by pre-faulting; faults and involuntary switches counted; residual tail attributed to preemption/interrupts

labs.title: Stride: the cache line is the unit of memory traffic
labs.evidence: 0.56 ns/access at stride 1, 4.3 ns at 64, 17.7 ns at 4096: three regimes named

labs.title: Working set: measure L1/L2/L3/DRAM and the STLB cliff by pointer chasing
labs.evidence: Staircase 2.4 / 4-12 / 24-82 / 128-184 ns matched to lscpu; the 8-16 MB step identified as page walks

labs.title: AoS vs SoA under field scan, all-fields and random access; the FP-chain trap
labs.evidence: SoA 2x on a field scan, 4.3x with -ffast-math (addsd chain proven in asm); AoS 2x on random records

labs.title: False sharing: independent counters on one line
labs.evidence: Adjacent counters 6x (2 threads) and 12x (4 threads) slower than padded; false sharing as costly as true sharing

labs.title: Memory-level parallelism; jump-pointer prefetch; when prefetch is useless
labs.evidence: 145 -> 12 ns/load with 16 chains; 140 -> 15 ns with jump pointers; 0% change on an index-array gather

labs.title: TLB reach and transparent huge pages (best-effort, measured)
labs.evidence: 147 -> 130 ns with full THP on 256 MB; 226 -> 189 ns with a third of 1 GiB huge (ENOMEM on collapse); miss rate 93% -> 65%

labs.title: What common C++ idioms compile to at -O2
labs.evidence: Twelve asm excerpts predicted then verified; zero() became jmp memset; dense switch became a result table

labs.title: Vectorization remarks: why a loop did or did not vectorize
labs.evidence: Seven remarks explained; dot 4x with reassociation; -march=native made scalar dot 2x slower via FMA (asm shown)

labs.title: llvm-mca: latency-bound vs throughput-bound, predicted then measured
labs.evidence: Predicted 4.0x, measured 4.5x; mca's over-charge of a fused load+add explained

labs.title: Branch vs cmov vs blend: the compiler chooses the shape, the data decides the cost
labs.evidence: Naive form compiled to a branch (7.3 ns random); load-both form vectorized (1.0-1.5 ns); compact via sbb trick

labs.title: Inlining across translation units: separate compilation vs LTO/ThinLTO, PGO recipe
labs.evidence: 1.32 -> 0.95 ns/call; the loop vectorized once scale() was visible; inline remark from lld captured

labs.title: A race the optimizer hides, a race that loses half the work, and TSan's report
labs.evidence: collapsed: one add per thread, 'passes'; racy: 2.0M of 4.0M; TSan flags both; atomic 39 ns, mutex 107 ns

labs.title: SPSC ring buffer three ways: seq_cst + false sharing vs acq/rel + padding vs cached indices; SMT siblings
labs.evidence: naive 148 ns/item; padded 18-42; cached 29-34 (stable); siblings 2.4 ns; TSan 0 warnings

labs.title: What each memory_order compiles to on x86-64, AArch64 v8.0 and LSE
labs.evidence: The 13-row table; only x86 seq_cst stores pay; Arm pays for anything above relaxed

labs.title: Mutex vs spinlock vs atomic, uncontended and contended, futex syscalls counted
labs.evidence: 25 / 13.5 / 11.8 ns uncontended; 0.6% of contended acquisitions reach the kernel

labs.title: The store-buffer litmus test: x86 reordering made visible
labs.evidence: relaxed 8.8%, acq/rel 24.6%, seq_cst 0% of 1M trials show r1==r2==0; seq_cst stores are xchg

labs.title: malloc as a distribution: tcache, bins, the dynamic mmap threshold, pools
labs.evidence: 36 / 52 / 41 ns medians; forced mmap 4.2 us p50 (200k mmap+munmap); pool 16 ns

labs.title: The syscall floor, the vDSO, VFS, scheduler entry, path lookup; strace's 100x
labs.evidence: vDSO 38 ns, getpid 142 ns, open+close 1.7 us; getpid 23.6 us under strace

labs.title: UDP round trip: blocking vs epoll vs busy-poll
Nagle + delayed ACK on write-write-read; TCP_NODELAY
labs.evidence: 41 ms p50 on 499/500 requests -> 41 us with one setsockopt

labs.title: Kernel receive timestamps: stack time vs wait time per packet
labs.evidence: wait p99 1.2 ms blocking -> 7.3 us spinning; stack time 2-5 us

labs.title: The same C on x86-64 and AArch64: calling convention, csel, mov+movk, stp/ldp, NEON in loops
labs.evidence: Seven functions side by side and the decoder ring

labs.title: NEON vs SVE codegen; one binary proven at five vector lengths under qemu
labs.evidence: n = 1003 correct at 128/256/512/1024/2048 bits; tail-folded loop has no remainder

labs.title: Exclusives vs LSE vs outline atomics; run on cortex-a57 and max
labs.evidence: LSE binary SIGILLs on a57; outline runs on both; the __aarch64_* link error and its fix

labs.title: Runtime dispatch: HWCAP, GNU ifunc, function pointers, and validating the choice
labs.evidence: Same binary picks dot_sve on max and dot_neon on a57 with identical results; IFUNC symbol shown

labs.title: SME first look: streaming mode, streaming VL, ZA tiles, one fmopa outer product
labs.evidence: Trace 10 / 36 / 136 at SVL 128 / 256 / 512; graceful 'no SME' on a57; smstart/fmopa in the asm

labs.title: Build topology: Ninja queries and the compile database on a 7,568-TU tree
labs.evidence: One compile line dissected; -O levels and -g counted across the tree; a single object reproduced by hand

labs.title: ELF forensics: PIE vs EXEC, static vs shared, stripped vs not, .symtab vs .dynsym, archives
labs.evidence: Distro clang = 157 KB launcher + 145 MB libLLVM.so; local clang = 209 MB static with 207k symbols; identification checklist filled for both

labs.title: Flags archaeology: .comment, DW_AT_producer, -frecord-command-line, build-id, clang -###
labs.evidence: The local clang was built by GCC 15 (from .comment); the exact driver line recovered from an object's .GCC.command.line

labs.title: The hot function is in a shared library you did not build: profile the compiler, avoid the two mis-profiles, map to source
labs.evidence: 71% libLLVM / 20% libclang-cpp / 8% libc with 11K samples; the ccache-hit and E-core mis-profiles shown and explained; FindNodeOrInsertPos mapped to SCEV uniquing

labs.title: Why does this file take three seconds to compile? -ftime-trace phases, instantiations, per-function optimizer time
labs.evidence: APInt.cpp: Backend 2.2 s of 3.1 s, one function 107 ms; heavy.cpp: std::regex instantiation 0.56 s

labs.title: Capstone 0 (worked): why does APInt.cpp take three seconds to compile, and what would make it faster?
labs.evidence: Two instruments agree: 3/4 optimizer+codegen; the experiment that follows is specified; the surprise line names the two wrong profiles

labs.title: Capstone 1 (template): a public x86 codebase, profile -> fix -> prove
labs.evidence: A write-up in the template with before/after tables, counters, asm diff, correctness evidence and a residual

labs.title: Capstone 2 (template): NEON vs SVE (and SME) kernel selection validated under emulation with a cost model
labs.evidence: Correctness matrix at four vector lengths; predicted cost per element per core; crossover size; dispatch with override
